newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut market bullish after hectic week.
newsitem.headline: Beirut market bullish after hectic week.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange appeared set for a bull run after Solidere surged to 20-month highs and bank shares traded at record levels in the week ended on Friday.
Brokers said Solidere should make easy gains next week as investors were likely to shift partially from the banking sector towards Lebanon's biggest company.

All three listed banks rose. Banque Audi jumped 8.5 percent to $28.5 for a 90 percent rise since listing in January, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose 5.73 percent to $20.75 and Bank of Beirut rose 2.85 percent to $4.5.
The LIBX bank index rose 5.05 percent to 180.42. The LISPI general index rose 3.63 percent to 93.99 and the BLOM general index rose 10.95 percent to 1074.75.
Market turnover doubled on the week to 1,858,225 shares from 928,235 for a value of $22,428,690 against $10,237,265.
Solidere A shares soared to $12.5 from $10.875 last week and B shares jumped to $12.5 from $11.25.
"We might see some switching out of the bank shares into Solidere, which I see gaining $2 easily within one month," Ziad Makkawi of Beirut finance house Middle East Capital Group said.
Thursday's news that Solidere planned to open up share ownership to foreign investors in October fuelled the surge by the company's shares.
"Clearly, there is increased interest in the market. A consolidation of bank prices would be healthy but I'm not sure we will see one. Every share is driving the others up," Makkawi said.

"I think we are getting to levels that might be a little bit expensive for bank shares. Audi at $28.5 is 3.5 times its book value based on 1996 figures and close to three times book value based on expected 1997 results."

Audi jumped 3.17 percent on Friday after it announced the acquisition for $50 million of medium-sized Credit Commercial du Moyen-Orient which has assets of $253 million, a 0.85 percent market share and eight branches.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was flat at $1.28125. There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic, pipemaker Eternit or Ciments Blancs.
